title: Good, but has some design shortcomings...
text:
Good, but has some design shortcomings.... My faithful [[ASIN:B0009VELTQ Cuisinart CBK-200 2-Pound Convection Automatic Breadmaker]] finally died after years of faithful service, so I was happy to be offered the Black and Decker B6000C Deluxe Bread Maker. I used my Cuisinart regularly to make yeast bread (white and whole wheat), sweet bread (on the dough setting), and jam. Because I am more familiar with the Cuisinart, I will use it as the basis for comparison here.

As I unboxed the B&D, I was surprised by how light the unit is (the Cuisinart had a metal body and lid). The unit is larger due to the shape of the pan and the fact that it bakes 3-pound loaves, but it does not have handles like the Cuisinart, which makes it difficult to move or put it away for storage. I was also a little dismayed to see that the large, heavy lid relies on a very small plastic hinge, which seems like it will crack / break sooner rather than later (the lid also tends to wobble a little when closed). The metal pan seems a bit thin, but I liked the fact that the two paddles are straight rather than curved like the Cuisinart. The B&D also seemed to do a better job at kneading due to the two paddles, but you'll still want to stop and scrape down the sides of the pan using a nonstick tool.

After getting the bread maker set up (I had to move it because the unit is tall and narrow and I could not open the lid fully because it kept hitting the underside of my cabinets), I used the included recipe to make a 3-pound loaf of herbed garlic French bread on the French cycle (setting 3). As other reviewers have mentioned, the LCD readout is a touch on the faint side, and may be difficult to read (my old Cuisinart did not have that problem and was easy to read from several feet away). I found I had to add extra liquid to the recipe, as the dough was far too dry at first and didn't come together, but the resulting loaf was moist and fluffy. I also liked the way the bread baked in the B&D; my Cuisinart tended to overbake everything, even on the "light" crust setting.

Here is one area where the Cuisinart excelled over the B&D manual: the Cuisinart bread machine includes dozens of recipes for each of the machine's settings, with ingredients scaled for 1, 1.5 and 2-pound loaves. The B&D manual only has ONE sample recipe for each setting, and the ingredients are automatically scaled for the largest 3-pound loaf size. Also, the Cuisinart listed the exact length of each step in the cycle for all of the settings; there are no times listed for the B&D. This can be problematic if you want to remove the paddles before the bread enters the baking cycle; the Cuisinart would beep before the final rise, but the B&D does not. Because there are no times listed in the manual, it takes a bit of guesswork (the LCD does underline which step of the baking process you are on).

Overall, I would still recommend the [[ASIN:B0009VELTQ Cuisinart CBK-200 2-Pound Convection Automatic Breadmaker]] for the many included recipes, variations, nutritional info, and design features, especially for new bakers. The B&D does turn out a decent loaf of bread, but the lack of included recipes (and scaled ingredients for smaller loaves), and more crucially the lack of knead and rise times, can make this less than user-friendly.

product_metadata.title: Black & Decker B6000C Deluxe 3-Pound Bread Maker, White
features: Crust control setting with automatic temperature adjustment for regular or dark crust
description: Enjoy fresh baked bread to your preference with the LCD display, audible signal for fruit and nut add ins, crust control, non-stick baking pan and large viewing window. To make things even easier you choose from 11 pre-programmed settings and choose up to a 13 hour bake delay.
